title: Scaling of entanglement with distance between subsystems: detection of phase transitions in the $t'$-$π$-flux model
authors: Maksim Ulybyshev, Gergő Roósz, Gabriele Bellomia, Karsten Held, Fakher Assaad, Frederic Bippus
abstract: The system-size scaling of bipartite entanglement can be used to detect phase transitions. We develop a related approach for strongly correlated electron models where large density matrices or large system size scaling are inaccessible. To this end, we demonstrate that phase transitions of various kinds are signaled by a sharp signature in the first- or second-order logarithmic derivatives of the negativity measuring entanglement between small clusters at varying distances. Crucially, we show how to mitigate the effect of quantum Monte Carlo noise at large distances when computing the negativity. Our focus is on the $t'$-$π$-flux Hubbard model using auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo simulations. It has the particular advantage of showing three distinct phase transitions in a single model: semimetal to band insulator, semimetal to antiferromagnetic Mott insulator, and a magnetic order-disorder transition belonging to the Gaussian, Gross-Neveu, and O(3) Wilson-Fisher universality classes, respectively.
summary: This work proposes using the scaling of fermionic entanglement negativity with distance as a robust diagnostic tool to detect quantum phase transitions in strongly correlated electron models. By applying this to the $t'$-$\pi$-flux Hubbard model via QMC, the authors successfully identify three distinct transitions, demonstrating the method's utility even when direct large-scale calculations are impossible.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of detecting phase transitions in strongly correlated electron models where standard methods fail due to computational limitations.
main_result: They demonstrate that phase transitions can be signaled by sharp signatures in the logarithmic derivatives of the fermionic negativity calculated between small, separated clusters.
method: The study uses auxiliary-field Quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) simulations combined with a novel diagnostic based on entanglement scaling with distance.
model_or_system: The primary model is the $t'$-$\pi$-flux Hubbard model on a square lattice, which is used to study three distinct phase transitions: SM to BI, SM to MI, and a magnetic order-disorder transition.
key_observables: Fermionic negativity ($\mathcal{N}_F$), first- and second-order logarithmic derivatives of negativity, and entanglement entropy ($S$).
important_parameters: The hopping parameters ($t, t'$), interaction strength ($U$), and the distance ($d$) between subsystems are key parameters.
main_assumptions: The approach assumes that the entanglement structure, specifically the negativity, is sensitive enough to reveal the underlying phase transition points even when full system-size scaling is intractable.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically presents the phase diagram of the $t'$-$\pi$-flux Hubbard model, illustrating the different phases (SM, BI, MI) and the transitions between them.
paper_structure: The paper develops a methodology to adapt entanglement detection from system-size scaling to distance scaling, applies this to the $t'$-$\pi$-flux Hubbard model using QMC, and analyzes the resulting signatures for three distinct phase transitions.
why_interesting: The technique provides a powerful, non-local diagnostic tool (entanglement scaling) to probe critical points in strongly correlated systems, which is highly relevant for understanding quantum materials.
